title: Le Passé Récent
description: venir de + infinitive: to have just done.

items.translation: Present of venir + de + infinitive = “have just…”
Imparfait of venir + de + infinitive = “had just…”
items.exampleFr: Elle venait de partir quand je suis arrivé.
items.exampleEn: She had just left when I arrived.

items.word: venir de + lieu / venir de + infinitif
items.translation: Before a place it means “come from”; before an infinitive, “have just”
items.exampleFr: Je viens de Paris. Je viens de rentrer.
items.exampleEn: I come from Paris. I have just come home.

items.prompt: Elle ___ de partir quand je suis arrivé.
Nous ___ de nous coucher quand le téléphone a sonné.
In French (passé récent): “I have just eaten.”
In French (passé récent): “She has just left.”
In French (passé récent): “We have just arrived.”
In French (passé récent): “They have just finished.”
In French (passé récent): “The train has just left.”
In French (passé récent): “I have just seen Paul.”
Which sentence is in the passé récent?
“Je vais manger” / “Je viens de manger” mean…
options: I am going to eat / I have just eaten
I have just eaten / I am going to eat
I go to eat / I come to eat
items.answer: I am going to eat / I have just eaten
